note: Which CMU joint drives which Paper Cinema bone. This is retargeting, not training: a recorded motion is a list of joint rotations per frame, so playing it on our skeleton is a name-to-name copy. No GPU, no model, no learning.
source: CMU Graphics Lab, subject 2 (swordplay). assets/mocap/CREDITS.md has the licence.
units: CMU AMC is degrees, our rig is radians. The loader converts.
axes: CMU is Y-up, Z-forward. figure.js is Y-up, -Z-forward, so Z flips (same as T() in modular_builder.py).

thorax.note: no separate thorax bone; fold 40% into the upper spine

lwrist.note: CMU splits wrist twist from the hand; lT is our forearm twist

dropped.ltoes: a folded-paper foot has no toe joint
dropped.rtoes: a folded-paper foot has no toe joint
dropped.lfingers: the hand is one folded piece; the grip is solved by gripHand() in figure.js

unmapped_ours.hakama: cloth, not a body joint: driven by the hip and thigh motion, not by capture data
